doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: Los Angeles and the West Coast
title: First important gigs: The Lighthouse and Shorty Rogers
summary: After San Diego clubs with Guerin and Sleet, he joined Howard Rumsey's Lighthouse All-Stars in 1962, then worked with Shorty Rogers and his Giants.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Right. What was the first important gig that, if you look back on it now, was there a series of gigs?

Probably — I worked at The Lighthouse, which was a really famous club and really an institution, in Hermosa Beach which is just south of Los Angeles on the coast there. It was called The Lighthouse All-Stars was the band. Howard Rumsey, who lives near here by the way now, in Hemet, which is a city about an hour and a half from San Diego, he had a wonderful band there, a house band there, I’m sure you’re familiar with The Lighthouse, and I was fortunate enough to play in that band for a few months in the — it would have been 1962 I guess. And before that I had just played around San Diego in clubs, with a lot of great players, a wonderful drummer named John Guerin, I don’t know if you’re familiar with his name, he’s been in L.A. for years, he was from down here, we grew up together. And a trumpet player who died very young unfortunately, named Don Sleet, who did some recording, a wonderful player. There were some marvelous young players down here. But the first job where I actually got out of San Diego and did something on the L.A. scene anyway was with that band at The Lighthouse. And then shortly thereafter I worked with Shorty Rogers and his Giants which was a very well known band in those days. And by that time I was pretty much settled in L.A. and playing up there mostly.
